claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 §15: "The first digit of the status code defines the class of response. ... There are five values for the first digit: 1xx (Informational): The request was received, continuing process; 2xx (Successful) ...; 3xx (Redirection) ...; 4xx (Client Error) ...; 5xx (Server Error)".
RFC 9110 §15: "a client MUST understand the class of any status code, as indicated by the first digit, and treat an unrecognized status code as being equivalent to the x00 status code of that class."
RFC 9110 §15.3.1: "The 200 (OK) status code indicates that the request has succeeded. The content sent in a 200 response depends on the request method." Table row GET: "the target resource".

RFC 9110 §15.3.2: "fulfilled and has resulted in one or more new resources being created." §9.3.3: "If one or more resources has been created on the origin server as a result of successfully processing a POST request, the origin server SHOULD send a 201 (Created) response".
RFC 9110 §15.3.5: "the server has successfully fulfilled the request and that there is no additional content to send in the response content."

RFC 9110 §15.4.2: "assigned a new permanent URI ... The server SHOULD generate a Location header field". §15.4.3: "resides temporarily under a different URI ... The server SHOULD generate a Location header field in the response containing a URI reference for the different URI."

RFC 9110 §15.4.5: "the client, which made the request conditional, already has a valid representation; the server is therefore redirecting the client to make use of that stored representation" and "A 304 response is terminated by the end of the header section; it cannot contain content or trailers."

RFC 9110 §15.5.1: "cannot or will not process the request due to something that is perceived to be a client error". §15.5.2: "lacks valid authentication credentials ... The server generating a 401 response MUST send a WWW-Authenticate header field". Caddyfile@stage-0 /admin: respond "Unauthorized: sign in at /login.html first" 401, no header directive.

RFC 9110 §15.5.4: "understood the request but refuses to fulfill it". §15.5.5: "did not find a current representation for the target resource or is not willing to disclose that one exists". §15.5.10: "could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the target resource."

RFC 9110 §15.6.1: "encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request". §15.6.3: "while acting as a gateway or proxy, received an invalid response from an inbound server". §15.6.4: "currently unable to handle the request due to a temporary overload or scheduled maintenance".

RFC 9112 §4: "The reason-phrase element exists for the sole purpose of providing a textual description associated with the numeric status code ... A client SHOULD ignore the reason-phrase content because it is not a reliable channel for information". RFC 9110 §15.1: "The reason phrases listed here are only recommendations".
RFC 9110 §15.5.4: "An origin server that wishes to \"hide\" the current existence of a forbidden target resource MAY instead respond with a status code of 404 (Not Found)."

RFC 9110 §15.5.2: "The user agent MAY repeat the request with a new or replaced Authorization header field". §15.5.4: "the server considers them insufficient to grant access. The client SHOULD NOT automatically repeat the request with the same credentials." "should not be expected to change the answer" stays within that SHOULD NOT.

Caddyfile@stage-0 :8080 route: @missingOrder 404, /redirect redir 302, /conflict 409, /slow 503 ("pretending to be overloaded"), /admin 401 fallback, file_server otherwise. outputs/stage-0/scripts/http/status-codes.txt@stage-0 is identical to the lesson output block (diff empty); a live run of the script printed the same seven codes.
Caddyfile@stage-0: handle /redirect { redir * /index.html 302 }. Live run: "HTTP/1.1 302 Found" then "Location: /index.html". RFC 9110 §15.4.3: server SHOULD generate Location for the different URI.
Caddyfile@stage-0 handle /admin: respond @guest ... 403; respond @signedIn ... 200; respond ... 401, with @guest header Cookie *role=guest*. Live run: "no cookie 401", "cookie role=guest 403".
Execution in the lab box (curl 8.21.0): -w "%{http_code}  $path" printed 200/302/404/401/409/503/404, matching each response status line; against a closed port it printed 000.

Execution: curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null .../redirect printed header lines only, no body. In the lab box, input lines "location: /x", "LOCATION: /y", "http/1.1 200", "X-Location: z" through grep -Ei '^(HTTP/|Location:)' kept the first three and dropped X-Location: case-insensitive, start-anchored.

status-codes.sh@stage-0 line 5: [ -f /.dockerenv ] || exec "$(dirname "$0")/../lab-run.sh" "$0" "$@". lab-run.sh@stage-0: exec docker compose exec -T lab bash -c 'exec bash "$0" "$@" 2>&1' "/repo/$rel".

RFC 9110 §15: "a three-digit integer code that describes the result of the request"; §15.3.1: 200 "indicates that the request has succeeded". §15 does not tie the code to the content; a 200 carrying a failure message contradicts §15.3.1. The recommendation is labelled as opinion.

Reproduced through the path lab-run.sh uses (docker compose exec -T lab bash -c '... 2>&1'), loop aimed at a closed localhost port, 5/5 runs: "curl: (7) Failed to connect ... Could not connect to server" comes FIRST, then "000  /index.html"; exit status 7, loop stops. curl stdout to a pipe is buffered until exit, stderr is not. Content right; the order the lesson states is not.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: With only the site stopped, curl cannot connect: it reports the failed connection, the loop prints 000  /index.html (curl's placeholder, not a status code), and set -euo pipefail ends the run there. With the whole lab down, the script fails before curl runs.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Opinion grounded in RFC 9110 §15.6.3: 502 = "while acting as a gateway or proxy, received an invalid response from an inbound server". §15.6.4 defines 503 as "the server is currently unable to handle the request" with no reference to an intermediary, so a 503 can originate at the proxy.

RFC 9110 §15.5.5: 404 = "the origin server did not find a current representation" — a response the server produced. Execution: with no listener curl exits 7 ("Could not connect to server") and no status line arrives (http_code 000).
RFC 9110 §15.5: "The 4xx (Client Error) class of status code indicates that the client seems to have erred." The lesson hedges with "seems" and "usually", matching the RFC wording.

RFC 9110 §15.4 lists "Redirects that indicate this resource might be available at a different URI, as provided by the Location header field, as in ... 301 (Moved Permanently), 302 (Found)" and "Redirection to a previously stored result, as in the 304 (Not Modified) status code."

issues.text: Order is the reverse of what the learner sees. Reproduced through lab-run.sh's own path (docker compose exec -T lab bash -c '... 2>&1', closed localhost port), 5/5 runs: "curl: (7) Failed to connect ..." is printed BEFORE "000  /index.html", because curl's stdout into a pipe is buffered until curl exits while stderr is not.
issues.quote: The loop prints `000  /index.html` — `curl`'s placeholder when no status line arrived, not a status code — then `curl` reports the failed connection and the script stops there.
issues.fix: Replace with: "`curl` reports the failed connection, and the loop prints `000  /index.html` — `curl`'s placeholder when no status line arrived, not a status code — then the script stops there." Set meta claim 21 text to this review's suggested_text.

issues.text: Meta claim 11 now uses version_key http_messaging (RFC 9112), but the frontmatter declares only http and caddy. docs/03: every lesson declares versions_used for the keys its claims depend on.
issues.fix: Change the frontmatter to versions_used: [http, http_messaging, caddy].

issues.text: Outline item 4 says a 5xx from a proxy (502/503) "usually means the app behind it is down or slow". The lesson limits that to 502 and says a 503 may come from the proxy itself, which RFC 9110 §15.6.4 supports. The lesson is right; the outline item is what should change. Already recorded as an owner open_question in meta.
issues.quote: a `503` may come from the proxy itself, so it says less about what is behind.
issues.fix: No lesson change. Owner: rewrite track.yaml outline item 4 to "A 502 comes from a proxy and points at the program behind it; a 503 can come from any server, including the proxy itself."

junior.reviewer: claude-opus-5-5 (junior reader simulation, prompt 05, round 1; known_vocab = 20 terms up to foundation.l1.http-request-response plus lesson vocab [proxy] and the prereq five-line summary)

issues.quote: repeating it with the same credentials should not be expected to change the answer.
issues.text: "credentials" is not in what I know and not in Core concepts. Everywhere else the lesson says "identity" (401 "carries no identity", the cookie "carrying who the caller claims to be"), so I cannot tell whether credentials is the same thing or something extra, like a password.
issues.fix: Replace "the same credentials" with "the same identity", matching the wording used for 401 in the same bullet and in section 5.

issues.quote: then `curl` reports the failed connection and the script stops there.
issues.text: Why does the script stop after the first address instead of printing 000 for all seven? The lesson never says what `set -euo pipefail` on line 3 does, so the "stops there" is a step I cannot reconstruct.
issues.fix: Add half a sentence: "because line 3, `set -euo pipefail`, ends the script at the first command that fails".

issues.quote: `304` says nothing has changed, so reuse the copy you already hold and read no body; a client may keep an earlier answer and ask whether it is still current.
issues.text: The clause that explains where the held copy comes from arrives after the instruction to reuse it. I read "the copy you already hold" first, got stuck, and only understood on the second read.
issues.fix: Swap the two halves: "a client may keep an earlier answer and ask whether it is still current; `304` says nothing has changed, so reuse that copy and read no body".

issues.quote: a `503` may come from the proxy itself, so it says less about what is behind.
issues.text: Section 4 defines 503 as "the server is not taking work at the moment". I cannot picture why a proxy that is up and answering would say that about itself, so the contrast with 502 stays half-understood (summary line 4 repeats it).
issues.fix: Add one clause after "the proxy itself": e.g. "when the proxy is too busy, or has been told to turn requests away".

issues.quote: You notice this when nothing ever retries and the orders quietly go missing.
issues.text: Who would retry? The bullet has not mentioned retrying; I had to guess that a client normally sends an order again after a failure code and does not after a 200.
issues.fix: Replace with: "You notice this when the client, seeing 200, never sends the order again, and orders quietly go missing."

issues.text: The prose explains `%{http_code}`, the thrown-away body and `-D -`, but not `-sS` or what `-w` itself does. I followed the line from the output, not from the prose.
issues.fix: Add a few words: "`-w` sets what `curl` prints after each request; `-sS` hides its progress output but keeps error messages".

issues.quote: `409` your request clashes with the current state of what is at that address.
issues.text: Every other 4xx code gets a picture later (the /admin pair, the two 404s), but 409 only appears as /conflict, "configured to answer that way". I cannot imagine a Đơn Hàng request that would clash with anything.
issues.fix: Add one short example in the 4xx sentence, e.g. "such as asking to cancel an order that has already been cancelled".
